info.title: Quantum Ready Labs API
info.summary: Post-quantum TLS readiness of a public host: a stage, a score, the one next step.
info.description: Open, no key. The scan opens TLS connections to the host you name, exactly as a browser visit would: fourteen handshakes and one ordinary connection. Only test hosts you are allowed to connect to. Results are kept for 24 hours and answered from that cache, each with a permanent share link and a PDF. Rate limits: 20 scans per caller address and 6 per host in any 10 minutes (429 with Retry-After). CORS is open (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *). Source: https://github.com/manteiga-foundation/quantum-ready-labs (MIT).

post.description: Default response is a stream of newline-delimited JSON events (application/x-ndjson): start, one probe per group or protocol, connection, result, saved. Send `Accept: application/json` to wait for the end and receive one JSON object instead. A fresh cached result (under 24 hours) is returned at once in both forms.

host.description: A host name or IP literal, optionally with :port. Only port 443 is scanned publicly.

schema.description: One JSON event per line: {type: 'start'|'probe'|'connection'|'result'|'saved'|'error', ...}. The `result` event carries a ScanResult; `saved` carries the share id.

400.description: Not a public host, an unsupported port, or malformed input.

502.description: The engine could not complete the scan.

get.description: The same scan as POST with `Accept: application/json`, for a shell or an agent: `curl 'https://quantumreadylabs.com/api/scan?host=example.com'`.

400.description: Not a public host or malformed input.

get.summary: The five-page PDF report for a result

200.description: application/pdf, landscape Letter, five pages; Content-Disposition names the file. The first render after a quiet spell can take up to 20 seconds; later ones are cached.

get.summary: The human page for a result
get.description: Unlisted (noindex), with Open Graph preview. Share this with people; share the JSON with machines.

Stage.description: exposed: TLS 1.3 is not available, sessions can be recorded today and decrypted later. at-risk: TLS 1.3 with forward secrecy and no post-quantum key exchange, safe today, harvestable. protected: hybrid post-quantum key exchange accepted. ready: protected, with no legacy key transport and short-lived automated certificates. unreachable / inconclusive: no TLS answer, or one the probes could not read with confidence.

cached.description: True when answered from a result under 24 hours old.

findings.description: Raw probe answers: groups (per key-exchange group: yes | no | error), tls13, tls12, rsaKeyTransport, preferredModernGroup, connection, chain, errors.

score.description: Quantum readiness only, not general TLS hygiene. Key exchange 60, foundations 30, certificate 10. See /docs/scoring.

foundations.description: Five booleans (null when not measured): tls13, noRsaKeyTransport, shortLivedCertificate, prefersHybrid, trustedChain.

points.description: The score's parts: keyExchange /60, noRsaKeyTransport /10, shortLivedCertificate /8, prefersHybrid /6, trustedChain /6, certificate /10.

code.description: A stable code for the same refusal (for example port-not-allowed, rate-caller, rate-host, no-address, not-public, engine-busy, invalid-host), so a client can say it in its own language.

params.description: The values the message names: host, port, allowed, address.
